The release links that intrusion to the Lazarus Group, which it describes as a North Korean state-sponsored group. The exchange's employee downloaded malware through an email, giving remote access, and the attackers used private keys to steal about $250 million in virtual currency. Tian and Li received about $91 million from DPRK-controlled accounts, plus $9.5 million from a second exchange hack. The release…

d8bf505e803d53fe7d7514c3fd8717ed60ba5259.summary: A U.S. Department of Justice press release (published 2018-08-01) announces federal indictments in Seattle against three alleged members of FIN7, also called the Carbanak Group and the Navigator Group. The report says FIN7 ran malware campaigns since 2015 against more than 100 U.S. companies, mainly in restaurants, gaming and hospitality, and sold the stolen card data. Three suspects were arrested abroad in 2018 (Germany, Poland, Spain) and are detained pending trial or extradition. The report says the charges are allegations and the defendants are presumed innocent.

d889f8ed2f6a73de74d4c8ec846a60281b64c951.summary: Cisco Talos report (published 2018-12-18) on illicit cryptocurrency mining. It links several groups, Rocke, the 8220 Mining Group and a group Talos named tor2mine, through shared tools, wallets and infrastructure. Methods include exploiting Apache Struts2, Oracle WebLogic, Drupal and Jenkins servers, malicious Git repositories, Pastebin-hosted scripts and XMRig miners. Rocke was observed developing destructive malware that poses as ransomware. The report estimates the groups hold about 1,200 Monero and earned hundreds of thousands of dollars combined.

d8c342f73b2603fedc4913e6a2378a846331fa96.summary: This is a Linux documentation page (a how-to on Linux kernel modules, LKMs) explaining how to insert and remove them with insmod, rmmod, modprobe and depmod, how module dependencies and loading errors work, and how /proc/modules is read. It describes no threat actor, campaign, malware, vulnerability or incident, so it is not a threat report.

d8141e5ae73b0856feae51f1c3dd07a979f15ad0.summary: RapperBot is an IoT malware family that Fortinet FortiGuard Labs has tracked since mid-June 2022. It reuses Mirai source code but mainly brute-forces SSH servers rather than Telnet. It has limited DDoS capability and adds persistence through SSH keys and a root account. The report says its primary motivation is still unclear.
